How They Handle Restricted Countries

When it comes to restricted countries, traditional digital commerce platforms often struggle to provide reliable services. Stripe and PayPal, for example, operate in only 46 countries out of 195 on earth, leaving a significant gap in coverage. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy may not be available or severely restricted in certain regions, making it difficult for creators to access these platforms. A sovereign commerce infrastructure, however, can be deployed in any region, providing a permanent structural alternative to traditional platforms. Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed, fees, and real costs, traditional digital commerce platforms often charge high fees and take a significant cut of sales revenue. A sovereign commerce infrastructure, on the other hand, charges a flat fee of 0.5% per transaction, making it a more cost-effective option for creators. Additionally, a sovereign commerce infrastructure provides instant payment verification and automatic webhook notifications, ensuring that creators can receive payment quickly and efficiently.
